71: Sealed - Their barrels were made of clay, and they would seal them with a clay stopper and coat them with mud around the seal to prevent the wine's aroma from escaping. In the months of Shevat or Nisan, when homeowners would sell barrels to shopkeepers—about ten or fifteen at a time—they would remove the seals, taste the wine, and then reseal them, applying mud around the stopper again. This process is called "rosham" (marking/sealing). The shopkeeper would then transport them to his home. Our Mishnah refers to a "marked barrel," which serves as a distinguishing sign, since some barrels are resealed (marked), while others are carried open to be sold immediately.
